snippets.text: ## Latest updates -- SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
Please check out our new release on [**Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2)**](https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything-2).
* SAM 2 code: https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything-2
![SAM 2 architecture](https://github.com/facebookresearch/segment-anything-2/blob/main/assets/model_diagram.png?raw=true)

**Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2)** is a foundation model towards solving promptable visual segmentation in images and videos. We extend SAM to video by considering images as a video with a single frame. The model design is a simple transformer architecture with streaming memory for real-time video processing. We build a model-in-the-loop data engine, which improves model and data via user interaction, to collect [**our SA-V dataset**](https://ai.meta.com/datasets/segment-anything-video), the largest video segmentation dataset to date. SAM 2 trained on our data provides strong performance across a wide range of tasks and visual domains.
# Segment Anything

[[`Paper`](https://ai.facebook.com/research/publications/segment-anything/)] [[`Project`](https://segment-anything.com/)] [[`Demo`](https://segment-anything.com/demo)] [[`Dataset`](https://segment-anything.com/dataset/index.html)] [[`Blog`](https://ai.facebook.com/blog/segment-anything-foundation-model-image-segmentation/)] [[`BibTeX`](#citing-segment-anything)]

The **Segment Anything Model (SAM)** produces high quality object masks from input prompts such as points or boxes, and it can be used to generate masks for all objects in an image. It has been trained on a [dataset](https://segment-anything.com/dataset/index.html) of 11 million images and 1.1 billion masks, and has strong zero-shot performance on a variety of segmentation tasks.

snippets.text: openpi holds open-source models and packages for robotics, published by the [Physical Intelligence team](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/).
Currently, this repo contains three types of models:
- the [π₀ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi0), a flow-based vision-language-action model (VLA).
- the [π₀-FAST model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/research/fast), an autoregressive VLA, based on the FAST action tokenizer.

- the [π₀.₅ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi05), an upgraded version of π₀ with better open-world generalization trained with [knowledge insulation](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/research/knowledge_insulation). Note that, in this repository, we currently only support the flow matching head for both $\pi_{0.5}$ training and inference.
- [Sept 2025] We released pi05, an upgraded version of pi0 with better open-world generalization.

- [Jun 2025]: We have added [instructions](examples/droid/README_train.md) for using `openpi` to train VLAs on the full [DROID dataset](https://droid-dataset.github.io/). This is an approximate open-source implementation of the training pipeline used to train pi0-FAST-DROID.

snippets.text: # Consistency Models

This repository contains the codebase for [Consistency Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.01469), implemented using PyTorch for conducting large-scale experiments on ImageNet-64, LSUN Bedroom-256, and LSUN Cat-256. We have based our repository on [openai/guided-diffusion](https://github.com/openai/guided-diffusion), which was initially released under the MIT license. Our modifications have enabled support for consistency distillation, consistency training, as well as several sampling and editing algorithms discussed in the paper.
The repository for CIFAR-10 experiments is in JAX and can be found at [openai/consistency_models_cifar10](https://github.com/openai/consistency_models_cifar10).

Consistency models are supported in [🧨 diffusers](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers) via the [`ConsistencyModelPipeline` class](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/consistency_models). Below we provide an example:
# https://github.com/openai/consistency_models/blob/main/scripts/launch.sh#L77

You can further speed up the inference process by using `torch.compile()` on `pipe.unet` (only supported from PyTorch 2.0). For more details, please check out the [official documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/main/en/api/pipelines/consistency_models). This support was contributed to 🧨 diffusers by [dg845](https://github.com/dg845) and [ayushtues](https://github.com/ayushtues).

snippets.text: openpi holds open-source models and packages for robotics, published by the [Physical Intelligence team](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/).
Currently, this repo contains three types of models:
- the [π₀ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi0), a flow-based vision-language-action model (VLA).
- the [π₀-FAST model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/research/fast), an autoregressive VLA, based on the FAST action tokenizer.

- the [π₀.₅ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi05), an upgraded version of π₀ with better open-world generalization trained with [knowledge insulation](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/research/knowledge_insulation). Note that, in this repository, we currently only support the flow matching head for both $\pi_{0.5}$ training and inference.
- [Sept 2025] We released pi05, an upgraded version of pi0 with better open-world generalization.

- [Jun 2025]: We have added [instructions](examples/droid/README_train.md) for using `openpi` to train VLAs on the full [DROID dataset](https://droid-dataset.github.io/). This is an approximate open-source implementation of the training pipeline used to train pi0-FAST-DROID.
| $\pi_0$      | Fine-Tuning | Base [π₀ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi0) for fine-tuning                | `gs://openpi-assets/checkpoints/pi0_base`      |

editorial.mechanism: 先把各实验室的轨迹变成统一数据格式，并以夹爪参考系中的位置、姿态和夹爪开合统一动作接口；未使用的动作分量按数据约定处理。RT-1-X 和 RT-2-X 在这个混合数据上训练，再与各机器人自己的专用数据策略比较。它检验的不是同一机器人多收点数据，而是别的机器人经验能否改善当前机器人。

studies.title: The Evaluation Protocol Determines the Result: An Independent Reproduction of LeWorldModel on TwoRoom
studies.identity_basis: Original paper lists the five LeWM authors; this report lists Joyjeet Singh (independent researcher; ORCID 0009-0005-1512-7439), with no author overlap. Public tinylab repository identifies LeWM reproduction from scratch.

protocol.evaluated_object: 18.03M-parameter LeWM TwoRoom reimplementation, plus the original authors released checkpoint evaluated by the same harness
protocol.original_method_baseline: JEPA world model and original squared-terminal-latent-distance CEM planning; author checkpoint and reproduced checkpoint share matched evaluation draws
protocol.training: Four GPU training runs; each checkpoint result uses one seed. Corrected hidden implementation conventions include normalized/z-scored inputs and action-block aggregation.
protocol.evaluation: 50 identical episodes per checkpoint/protocol cell in a CPU harness; repository goal offset25/action budget50 versus appendix goal offset100/action budget150; CEM300 candidates/30 refinements/30 elites, planning horizon5, frameskip5
protocol.method_changes: The corrected reimplementation repairs fidelity deviations rather than adding a new planner cost. Separate goal-construction and budget interventions vary evaluation protocol with weights held fixed.
protocol.source_locator: §2 scope; §3/Table1 fidelity; §4 protocol; §5/Table3 one-step error versus planning

repository_protocol.original_paper_report: approximately87%; different published protocol ambiguity addressed by study

results.goal_construction_only: Original author weights: repository goal construction84% versus recorded-target construction8%
results.representation: Position probe Pearson r approximately0.9988 versus original approximately0.996
results.interpretation: Independent reproduction of selected representation/planning claims and investigation of protocol sensitivity; does not reproduce the entire original experiment suite

limitations: Single environment and seed for each checkpoint/protocol result
Four training runs do not equal four independent groups or four statistical seeds
Evaluation protocol ambiguity and implementation corrections constrain direct comparison with the original approximately87%
No new robot or zero-shot embodied evaluation
Experiments are authors reported; not independently rerun in this task

studies.title: The Objective Is the Bottleneck: Latent World Models Encode What Their Planners Cannot Use

protocol.evaluated_object: Same TwoRoom LeWM checkpoints from the preceding independent reproduction, including original author weights
protocol.original_method_baseline: Frozen encoder/dynamics and squared-terminal-latent-distance CEM; matched baseline episodes and seed
protocol.method_changes: Replaces only terminal scoring with a fitted position probe or learned temporal-distance head. The world model is not retrained, but probes/metric heads are fitted; this is not a learning-free intervention.
protocol.evaluation: 50 matched episodes per cell; offset100/action budget150 main long-horizon comparison, with offset25/budget50 and shorter-budget checks
protocol.source_locator: §2 protocols; §4 latent objective diagnosis; §5 learned terminal costs; report conclusion

results.interpretation: Follow-up mechanism experiment from the same independent group; new cost outcomes are not original LeWM success rates

limitations: Same author/group as 2608.10145; count once for independence
Probe/head quality and checkpoint interact strongly
TwoRoom only; no claim of general robot-task reproduction
No world-model retraining still permits fitting auxiliary probe/head
Experiments are authors reported; not independently rerun here

studies.title: World Model Control by Trajectory Reachability Metrics
studies.identity_basis: Current v2 author/affiliation block: Liangyu Li, Shengzhi Wang, Mingliang Xiong, Qingwen Liu at Tongji; Libin Qiu at Alibaba. No author overlap with original LeWM or Joyjeet Singh; this is a distinct experimental group.

protocol.evaluated_object: Public frozen LeWM TwoRoom checkpoint family tworoom_aligned_e10_h1_go25_b50, latent dimension192, 512 projections, seeds3072/3073/3074; original LeWM PushT artifact also examined
protocol.checkpoint_provenance: Appendix C.1 cites immutable upstream model revision77adaae0bc31deab21c93740d1f8bb947cd0bdec and dataset revision6903a2de048b13819d812da0b4dd661290bc01e4 at quentinll/lewm-tworooms; exact expanded cache SHA256ee3218700ddbcc2d0e8c810a357e5ce2d3b610323f44a52bbf91d4296c4a98a7
protocol.original_method_baseline: Frozen LeWM encoder/predictor with raw terminal latent MSE and the same CEM action sampler, optimizer, evaluation set and budget. Its measured7.0% belongs to this new high-distance manifest, not to the original LeWM paper benchmark.
protocol.method_changes: Post-hoc TRM terminal cost: train a two-hidden-layer256-unit pairwise MLP on same-episode temporal separations using100000 balanced full-horizon pairs. Hold encoder, dynamics, sampler, optimizer, evaluation manifest and budget fixed; only scalar terminal ranking changes.
protocol.evaluation: 100 closed-loop episodes per seed:50 same-room +50 cross-wall, 47 cross-wall goals need the doorway; seeds3072/3073/3074; CEM300 candidates,10 iterations,30 elites;50executed-action budget
protocol.episode_exclusion: Before sampling train and validation temporal pairs, exclude all200 evaluation start/goal rows and the193 source episodes. Measured row overlap0 and episode overlap0; world model/checkpoints and manifest remain fixed.

results.unit: success percent, mean ± sample standard deviation across 3 frozen-checkpoint seeds,100 episodes each
results.paired_sign_flip_test: p=.25 across3 checkpoints; study does not claim conventional significance from this smallKtest
results.interpretation: Independent experimental re-evaluation of public LeWM checkpoints and a new terminal-cost repair.96.7% is TRM under episode exclusion, not original LeWM performance. Full-cache97.0% is a separately labeled reference.

limitations: External-check coverage of selected TwoRoom/PushT objects, not reproduction of all original LeWM experiments
TRM uses learned auxiliary temporal head and in-domain logged data; no zero-shot environment-transfer claim
Public source is a preprint; its author-reported protocol/results are verified against text, not rerun in this task
The paper describes a Code and Data Supplement; no independently verified external release URL was exposed in current HTML
Single-checkpoint layout probes: moved doorway partial transfer, rotated wall failure
PushT exposes ranking-versus-closed-loop limits in contact-rich control

snippets.text: openpi holds open-source models and packages for robotics, published by the [Physical Intelligence team](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/).
Currently, this repo contains three types of models:
- the [π₀ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi0), a flow-based vision-language-action model (VLA).
- the [π₀-FAST model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/research/fast), an autoregressive VLA, based on the FAST action tokenizer.

- the [π₀.₅ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi05), an upgraded version of π₀ with better open-world generalization trained with [knowledge insulation](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/research/knowledge_insulation). Note that, in this repository, we currently only support the flow matching head for both $\pi_{0.5}$ training and inference.
- [Sept 2025] We released pi05, an upgraded version of pi0 with better open-world generalization.

- [Jun 2025]: We have added [instructions](examples/droid/README_train.md) for using `openpi` to train VLAs on the full [DROID dataset](https://droid-dataset.github.io/). This is an approximate open-source implementation of the training pipeline used to train pi0-FAST-DROID.
| $\pi_0$      | Fine-Tuning | Base [π₀ model](https://www.physicalintelligence.company/blog/pi0) for fine-tuning                | `gs://openpi-assets/checkpoints/pi0_base`      |
